title: Keeping a pet in a rented apartment
question: Can I keep a pet in a rented apartment in Poland?
short_answer: Polish law does not prohibit pets in rentals, but the landlord can add a no-pets clause to the contract. Always check your lease agreement before bringing a pet.
conditions: Check your lease (umowa najmu) — if there is no pets clause, you are generally allowed
If the lease says 'no pets' (zakaz trzymania zwierząt) — you need written permission from the landlord
Best practice: always get written consent from the landlord before bringing a pet
You are responsible for any damage caused by your pet
Landlord can include a higher deposit (kaucja) if you have pets
exceptions: Guide dogs and assistance animals cannot be banned — this is protected by Polish disability law
Some housing cooperatives (spółdzielnia) have their own internal rules about pets
If you break a no-pets clause: landlord may terminate the lease with 1 month notice
penalties: Breach of no-pets lease clause: landlord can claim damages from deposit
